page0: The developer needs a clear feed of what is entering MOOR and what is actually added to the right pipeline because multiple workers/chats operate in parallel and the developer cannot perfectly remember everything. Keep the presentation extremely simple: timestamped text feeds for different trackers, click an event for receipts, evidence, statistics, artifacts, or a place to review the work.
objective: Create a read-only, low-noise owner HMI in Pulse that composes append-only worker events and existing repository trackers into multiple timestamped text streams, making semantic pipeline progress and visibility gaps obvious without turning the feed into project-management software.

live_sources: linked Funnel receipts, blueprints and CI evidence
streams: Repository — live PR and commit activity

owner_visibility_rule: Technical completion and owner visibility are separate states. A change is owner-visible only when the developer can locate it from Dev Feed or its explicitly named canonical destination and follow evidence links.
worker_rule: Every future material build/change should emit unique append-only Dev Feed event receipts at meaningful state transitions. Repository activity remains an independent source of truth and can expose missing semantic events.
done_criteria: Developer can see timestamped events in multiple clean streams.
Clicking an event exposes source, worker, stage, destination, details, evidence/receipt refs and available statistics.
Parallel workers can add events without editing one shared append-only file.
GitHub PR/commit activity appears independently so silent worker omissions remain detectable.
Feed flags artifact-exists-not-in-Pulse and merged-not-owner-visible gaps.
Trajectory is registered in Pulse so the known visibility gap is repaired.
Dev Feed itself is registered and preserved across Pulse rebuilds.
The sealed Funnel verifies the Dev Feed blueprint before execution.
honest_limits: Browser GitHub API polling is near-real-time, not push/WebSocket streaming.
A worker that never creates a semantic event can still appear through repository activity after it opens a PR or pushes/merges, but pre-repository private chat work cannot be observed automatically.
Dev Feed is read-only observability; it does not grant build/release authority.
